    Guide

    Recording setup for instructors

    Microphones, lighting and the settings that make a difference.

    What is inside

    Microphones, lighting and the settings that make a difference. It is written to be used, not read once: every page is a step you can run this week with your own work.

    • The short version, on one page
    • The full checklist with examples
    • A blank version to fill in

    Who it is for

    Designers, engineers and instructors who want a repeatable process rather than another opinion.

    Download

    4 pages · Sample PDF · PDF

    Updated September 2026

    Download sample PDF

    A real sample PDF, free to download. No account, email or tracking.

    • No account needed
    • Print-friendly
    • Reusable in client work

    An accessible, readable alternative

    The workbook, right here.

    The same text as the downloadable PDF, available without a PDF reader.

    01 / Understand the task

    Microphones, lighting and the settings that make a difference.

    Make a short teaching recording that is intelligible, readable and easy to follow.

    Choose one small, real example to work on. A focused attempt gives you better evidence than a general impression.

    Your example: ____________________________________________________________

    Your audience: ___________________________________________________________

    Your intended outcome: ___________________________________________________

    One constraint: __________________________________________________________

    02 / Put a method to work

    1. Choose a quiet room and record a ten-second voice test.

    2. Place the microphone consistently; reduce room noise before adding processing.

    3. Use soft light facing you, not a bright window behind you.

    4. Enlarge demonstration text and hide unrelated notifications.

    5. Record one clear explanation, one example and one small learner task.

    6. Review the exported sound and image; supply captions or a transcript.

    Working notes: __________________________________________________________

    _________________________________________________________________________

    03 / A worked practice scenario

    Test sentence: "Today we will make one small change, check it, then explain why it helped."

    Listen for clipping, hum, echo and changes in level. Watch whether the cursor and demonstration text are easy to follow.

    The theme room controls are simulations. Use your real recording software and device settings for an actual microphone test.

    Apply the method to your own example. What changes?

    Your first attempt: _______________________________________________________

    Your revision: ___________________________________________________________

    04 / Reflect and keep going

    Can a learner understand the lesson without perfect hearing, a large screen or prior tool knowledge?

    What is clearer after using this workbook?

    _________________________________________________________________________

    What evidence supports that conclusion?

    _________________________________________________________________________

    What is the smallest useful next step?

    _________________________________________________________________________

    Feedback prompt: "I noticed ____. That helped / made it harder to ____. One thing to try is ____."

    You may adapt this original sample workbook for personal learning and classroom demonstrations.

    This is sample learning material, not legal, financial, medical or accreditation advice.
